faq.q: What temperature scales does the converter support?
faq.a: Our temperature converter supports four major temperature scales: Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F), Kelvin (K), and Rankine (°R). You can convert between any of these scales with high precision and instant results.

faq.q: How accurate are the temperature conversions?
faq.a: The temperature conversions are mathematically precise using standard conversion formulas. Our converter provides high decimal precision suitable for scientific, educational, and professional applications with accurate results every time.

faq.q: What's the difference between Celsius and Fahrenheit temperature scales?
faq.a: Celsius uses water's freezing point (0°C) and boiling point (100°C) as references, making it intuitive for scientific use. Fahrenheit uses 32°F for water's freezing point and 212°F for boiling point, commonly used in the United States.

faq.q: When should I use Kelvin for temperature conversion?
faq.a: Kelvin is the SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature, commonly used in scientific calculations, physics, and chemistry. It starts at absolute zero (0 K = -273.15°C) and is essential for scientific research and engineering applications.

faq.q: Can the temperature converter handle negative temperatures?
faq.a: Yes, our temperature converter accurately handles negative temperatures for all supported scales. This includes sub-zero Celsius and Fahrenheit temperatures, as well as very low Kelvin values for scientific applications.

faq.q: How do I convert Fahrenheit to Celsius quickly?
faq.a: To convert Fahrenheit to Celsius: subtract 32, then multiply by 5/9. For example, 68°F = (68-32) × 5/9 = 20°C. Our converter automates this calculation instantly for any temperature value.
